purpose: Regression tests for causal debugging behavior. Each case contains tempting but insufficient correlation evidence; a good run reconstructs provenance and proves a mechanism before proposing remediation.

evals.prompt: A test started failing today. There are two commits in the last hour: the newest changes comments/docs in the failing file, the earlier commit changes a default consumed by the failing call path. Diagnose and propose the fix.
must: establish a last-known-good / first-known-bad window or equivalent evidence
inspect recent commit bodies and diffs rather than blaming the newest commit
identify the causal change only after its mechanism explains the failure
preserve the original valid intent in the proposed remediation
must_not: declare the newest commit causal from timestamp/path proximity alone
stack speculative fixes before a falsifiable hypothesis

evals.prompt: A deployment immediately precedes a production error. The deployed commit correctly enables a previously-unused code path, but the null-handling bug inside that path predates the commit by months. Perform the RCA.
must: reconstruct why the enabling change was made from commit/PR/Issue evidence when available
trace to the older defective assumption
avoid reverting the valid enabling change unless evidence shows that is the correct containment action
must_not: equate deploy correlation with source root cause
erase the valid behavior the deployment was intended to add without discussing that contract

evals.prompt: A recent refactor appears to correlate with a latency regression. Reverting it makes the benchmark fast again, but its commit body and linked Issue show it fixed a data-loss bug. Decide what to do.
must: treat the revert as evidence/experiment rather than the final fix
record the original data-loss contract as a constraint
profile or otherwise prove the new latency mechanism
propose a change that preserves the data-loss fix while removing the measured bottleneck
verify both correctness and performance afterward
must_not: ship the revert solely because performance improves
optimize without a measured baseline and post-change comparison

evals.prompt: Grafana shows errors in service C after a deploy to service A. Service Graph shows A -> B -> C; Tempo bad traces first become abnormal in B, while C only reports the downstream failure. Prometheus confirms B latency changed at deploy time. Identify the investigation plan.
must: use topology to traverse upstream rather than treating C as the root because it alerts
correlate Grafana/Prometheus/Tempo over the same incident window
connect the first abnormal span to the deployed artifact and its change provenance
require a causal mechanism before attributing the incident to the deployment
must_not: treat a single dashboard panel or alert as sufficient RCA evidence
